title: EXP-015 — Verify Form Variable Serialization After Ordinary Save
objective: Create one new User-scope classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_FormVariableLab05, add exactly one Form variable named FX_SerializationProbeVar with Global=False, Persistent=True, and Value=Seed-Serialize-E, record its complete visible design-time definition, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save, and then inspect the saved Form through a supported independent Form-definition representation that exposes Form-variable metadata. Determine whether the saved representation contains the exact variable definition. After that serialization evidence is captured, perform one ordinary clean Form-tab close/reopen and compare the reopened Details > Variables state with both the pre-Save baseline and the independent saved-definition evidence. The experiment must distinguish 'never serialized by Save' from 'serialized but not recovered after reopen' without using direct database access, undocumented APIs, cache manipulation, or runtime variable execution.

acceptance_checks.description: Before mutation, evidence proves a live server-backed Mongoose workflow, User editing scope, and zero exact/case-insensitive Name matches for FX_FormVariableLab05.
Evidence proves exactly one User-scope classic BuildFromScratch FX_FormVariableLab05 was created using Save Template unchecked and is open clean before variable creation.

Before Save, Details > Variables visibly contains exactly one FX_SerializationProbeVar and captured evidence records all visible definition fields, including Global=False, Persistent=True, and Value=Seed-Serialize-E.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Save succeeds, the Designer returns to a demonstrably clean state, and the same variable remains visibly unchanged immediately afterward; this check is explicitly classified as client-side visibility only, not persistence proof.

Before any Form close/reopen, a supported independent saved-Form representation is captured and proves either (a) FX_SerializationProbeVar is present with matching defining values in the serialized Form definition, or (b) it is demonstrably absent from that representation. If no supported independent representation can be reached, the experiment stops blocked rather than substituting internal APIs or client state.
After AC-5 evidence is captured, the clean target Form is closed exactly once through the ordinary Designer Form-tab close control with no unsaved-change prompt.
The Form is reopened exactly once through a supported Designer reopen path, and evidence proves Name=FX_FormVariableLab05 plus ScopeType=User and the same ScopeName as baseline.

Post-reopen Details > Variables is captured and compared against the pre-Save baseline and AC-5 saved-definition evidence, allowing an observable classification of 'serialized and recovered', 'serialized but not recovered', or 'not shown serialized before close'. No causal mechanism is inferred.

Controlled-action audit proves exactly one ordinary Save, one close, one reopen, no Regenerate/Save As, no cache/global-object/IDO-metadata action, no runtime execution, and no login/Sign In-OK/deliberate reauthentication/session replacement after Form creation began.

Repository/worktree evidence shows experiment-attributable changes are confined to the EXP-015 record and evidence/EXP-015/, with no recipe, AGENTS.md, environment, other experiment, existing FX_, or non-FX_ artifact modified.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261003-215618-zZRS. Rationale: EXP-013 and EXP-014 both showed a Global=False, Persistent=True variable remaining visible and unchanged in the still-open Designer immediately after a successful ordinary Save request, while EXP-014 then showed zero variables after close/reopen. The missing fact is whether ordinary Save ever serialized the variable definition into the saved Form metadata. This experiment uses a new FX_ Form and a supported independent Form-definition representation, such as FormSync comparison/export/pseudo-code where available, to isolate serialization before introducing another close/reopen boundary. This is a new documented diagnostic approach, not a replay or repair of blocked EXP-014.
